name: Klausism
summary: The political outlook of Václav Klaus, founder of the Czech Civic Democratic Party: radical free-market liberalisation, privatisation and a small state, combined with defence of the nation state against European integration, hostility to environmentalism and climate policy, opposition to mass migration and multiculturalism, and cultural conservatism on family and gender. Klaus presents it as classical liberalism in economics and conservatism in culture, against what he calls Europeism and the post-democratic 'isms'.
scope: Klaus's own articulated doctrine, 1989-2026: his speeches and essays on klaus.cz (Europeism, transition, climate, migration, the nation state) and Prushankin's scholarly analysis of his early texts. Excludes other ODS platforms, 'Klausism without Klaus' politicians, and the practice of his governments, which ruled in coalition and compromised (retained welfare, rent caps); only his stated positions are used.

notes: Based on 16 sources, mostly Klaus's own English-language speeches. Themes searched: economy and welfare, tax and spending, trade and aid, EU integration and the euro, nation state, democracy, migration and multiculturalism, family and gender, climate and environment, NATO and geopolitics, communism. Searched without finding a position: healthcare, minimum wage, unions, drugs, abortion, death penalty, policing, courts, voting systems, religion and state, race, animals, technology (nuclear, AI). Klaus's 2026 Oxford speech says it is wrong to fight communism now, which sits against his earlier anti-communism, so defeat-communism is left null. Klaus's governments (coalition, 1992-97) kept social protection; this is not treated as the ideology's record. Climate claims are Klaus's political position, not a scientific finding.
